old_problem: The Items field names an E1.S hot-plug functional check, while every executable line selects FAN records and the source defines neither a physical stimulus nor before/during/after observations. A steady FAN snapshot cannot prove E1.S insertion/removal detection, presence transition, event generation, link recovery or storage integrity. Conversely, an E1.S presence sensor need not contain `FAN`. The DeepSeek proposal substitutes a guessed literal name and incomplete evidence rather than resolving this mismatch.
disposition_reason: Retain Engineering Decision Pending and Source Conflict because neither ED-01 through ED-30 nor standard IPMI command semantics can decide which competing Master scope is authoritative. The project owner must choose E1.S hot-plug sensor resources, associated FAN resources, or two separately accepted checkpoints and supply a causal device-to-fan/sensor map. Runtime target identifiers and signed sensor values are parameterizable, so the row is not irreducibly BLOCKED. Until the scope ruling exists, the Review layer authorizes only complete read-only IB/OOB SDR and Sensor collection; it does not invent an E1.S removal/insertion step. If actual hot-plug coverage is required, it must be a separate operator-controlled, safety-reviewed case with workload/data protection, transition oracle and recovery.
decision_basis: The exact XLSX row 1663, same-row DeepSeek/test-json content, GPT V2, historical V3.1 record, pending/conflict analyses, duplicate identity result and ED-01 through ED-30 rules were read. The actual next formal queue identity was reconstructed and directly opened as Functionality row 1672 / Wistron-BMC-00943-V002 / a659fdbf7cac0ddf.

Standard `ipmitool sdr elist` and `ipmitool sensor list` semantics support read-only inventory collection, but they cannot establish that a FAN record represents the E1.S device, its presence signal or its hot-plug behavior. That relationship is platform/OEM topology authority, not a Linux/IPMI default.

The source supplies four evidence planes—IB SDR, OOB SDR, IB Sensor and OOB Sensor—but filters each by `FAN`. `grep FAN` may be used only as a discovery aid after canonical IDs are approved; a string match cannot define the required population or prove causality.

A functional hot-plug claim requires defined pre-state, authorized stimulus, transition timing, expected sensor/event/link/storage outcomes and safe recovery. None exists in this row, so adding physical removal/insertion would expand coverage into an unreviewed hardware action rather than repair the testcase.

The generic log-clear boilerplate is excluded: historical evidence must be preserved, and an empty log created by deletion is not proof that the transition was healthy. No fan speed, threshold, event enable, device state or log may be changed.

The owner can bind exact BMC/SUT identity, canonical resources, device-to-fan/sensor associations, units, thresholds, freshness and allowed discrepancies at runtime. Those missing values count as Project SPEC requirements but do not justify BLOCKED while the safe collection contract is known.

ED-02/ED-03/ED-13 allow parameterized standard read-only BMC work; ED-17/ED-25 keep any physical hardware operation human-controlled and separately governed; ED-18 forbids invented thresholds; ED-19 preserves evidence before deletion; ED-21/ED-24 preserve identity and visual/manual boundaries; ED-26 forbids automatic retry; ED-33/ED-35/ED-36/ED-38 preserve Master/coverage and separate review from execution/verdict.

test_case.test_name: Sensor check — unresolved E1.S hot-plug versus FAN scope with read-only IB/OOB evidence
test_case.purpose: Preserve both original candidate scopes while preventing a FAN name match from being reported as proof of E1.S hot-plug behavior. After the owner supplies the authoritative scope and topology, collect complete same-target SDR and live Sensor views through IB and OOB and compare each approved resource to the signed platform matrix without changing hardware or logs.
required_package: Written owner ruling selecting E1.S hot-plug sensor resources, E1.S-associated FAN resources, or separate checkpoints; original Source Key and Variant ID remain attached
Verified SUT/BMC/firmware identity plus canonical E1.S device, slot, fan, SDR entity/record and live Sensor association map with causal basis
Signed platform SPEC for required resource IDs/names/descriptions, units/scaling, expected readings or discrete states, thresholds/status, freshness, absent-state semantics and IB/OOB equivalence
Supported `ipmitool`, protected credential handling, same-target IB/OOB proof, complete untruncated collectors and immutable evidence destination

If physical hot-plug is later required: a separate approved case defining operator role, workload/data protection, device eligibility, stimulus, timing, event/link/storage oracles and validated recovery
test_case.test_command: Only after the written scope/map is supplied, capture complete untruncated output from the same verified target for IB `ipmitool sdr elist`, IB `ipmitool sensor list`, OOB `ipmitool sdr elist`, and OOB `ipmitool sensor list`; hash the raw evidence, normalize record identity/entity/association/name/description/reading/unit/status/threshold/freshness, and compare only the owner-approved resources to the signed matrix. A `FAN` filter may annotate discovery but must not truncate canonical evidence or define scope. Do not run the DeepSeek literal-title query, clear logs, change fan/sensor state, or perform E1.S removal/insertion in this testcase.
test_case.expected_result: For the owner-approved read-only checkpoint, every required mapped resource appears exactly once in all applicable evidence planes, resolves to the same physical E1.S/fan relationship, and matches the signed name/description/value-or-state/unit/status/threshold/freshness rules; IB and OOB observations are reconcilable within approved timing. The collection causes no device, fan, threshold, event-enable, BMC or log mutation. No result from this row alone is represented as proof of physical hot-plug behavior unless a separate governed stimulus case is approved and executed.
test_case.pass_fail_basis: Review remains PENDING until the owner resolves the competing E1.S/FAN scopes and signs the association/oracle. After binding, PASS evidence for the read-only checkpoint requires all four complete views and per-resource matrix conformance; command exit zero, non-empty `grep FAN`, a guessed literal name, partial/truncated output or unspecified threshold is insufficient. Missing, extra, duplicate, stale or divergent records and unsupported associations are reported for engineer FAIL/BLOCKED disposition. The end user owns the verdict; no hardware PASS is claimed here.
safety_gate: Do not infer that a FAN-labelled record proves E1.S presence, removal/insertion or hot-plug health; stop when scope or association is unsigned.
Do not physically remove/insert E1.S, disconnect cables, change fan speed, thresholds/event enables, storage workload or any device state under this row.
Do not clear SEL, SDR or other logs; retain the first inconsistent evidence and do not automatically retry to obtain a matching snapshot.
Verify exact same-target IB/OOB identity and protect credentials; reject cross-host, cached, truncated or `head`-limited output.
Do not invent OEM sensor names, mappings, units, thresholds, timing windows or unsupported-feature N/A determinations.
expected_evidence: Exact Source Key/Variant ID, written scope ruling and signed E1.S-device-to-fan/sensor association matrix
SUT/BMC/firmware/ipmitool identity, same-target IB/OOB proof and collection timestamps
Immutable hashes plus complete raw IB SDR, OOB SDR, IB Sensor and OOB Sensor outputs
test_case.recovery: The authorized path is read-only. On target mismatch, incomplete output, missing mapping, divergent evidence or BMC instability, stop, retain the first raw evidence and close protected sessions; do not clear, retry, reset or manipulate hardware. Because this row authorizes no hot-plug or fan change, no physical recovery may be improvised. Any later stimulus case must carry its own validated reinsertion/link/storage/service recovery and abort procedure.
